topic: Most fossils are stone, not bone
script: Most dinosaur fossils are not bone anymore, they are stone. Only a tiny fraction of living things ever become fossils. Most fossils form when remains are buried quickly in mud or sand. Over time, minerals in water fill and replace the bone. Footprints, eggs, skin and even poop can fossilize too. Scientists often date fossils by dating the volcanic ash layers around them.
